Grange School, Ikeja, and St Saviour’s School, Ikoyi, won overall titles at the second Pan African School Games, held at James Hope College, Lekki. Grange School won the Under 13 and Under 15 categories, while St Saviour’s School took the Under 11 title in the three-day tournament, which drew more than 400 students from 11 schools. Grange School received a new bus sponsored by Mikano Changan Motors for finishing with the most points. In the Under 11 category, St Saviour’s School won swimming and athletics, and shared the football title with Lagos Preparatory & Secondary School. Grange School won swimming and athletics in both the Under 13 and Under 15 categories, while Riverbank School won football in both age groups. Seun Akinbohun, Busola Tejumola and Aderoju Ope Ajayi organised the Games. Sponsors included Prime Atlantic, Zenith Bank, Plumtre Advisory, Mikano Changan Motors, UAC Foods, Nigerian Exchange Group, Team 33 Productions, Flytime, What Media, Kantar, Logic City and Flutterwave. The Lagos State Government and the Lagos State Sports Commission also supported the event. ‎Lagos backs sports campaigns against drug abuse, mental health issues Young swimmers shine at 2nd Pan-African School Games Pan African Games begin with school bus up for grabs The commission’s Director of Sports, Travih Nunayon, who represented Director General Lekan Fatodu, said talent scouts had been deployed to identify promising athletes. He said athletes identified at the Games could be considered for the National Youth Games and the National Intermediate Games, and that the commission would keep monitoring their progress. He added that talks had begun with the organisers on sustaining the initiative. Ope Ajayi, who is also Chairman of the Lagos State Aquatics Association, said the Games were set up to help children develop their sporting potential alongside their education. She said the founders, who are also sports parents, understood the opportunities sport can bring, including scholarships. “We want children to look back and say this is where I was discovered, this is where I got a scholarship opportunity, and this is where I had my opportunities,” she said. Participants and coaches praised the organisers and hoped future editions would bring in more schools. Peter Akinbo Peter, who has been covering sports for PUNCH for close to two years, focuses on combat sports reporting, special features and human angle stories
